author: "Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James" (1:1). Traditionally he is the Judas named among Jesus' brothers, alongside James (Matthew 13:55, Mark 6:3).
recipients: "Them that are sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called" (1:1): believers the letter does not locate, among whom false teachers had "crept in unawares" (1:4).

date.traditional: About AD 65-80, by Jude the brother of James and of Jesus.
date.scholarly: Views range from the 50s to the early second century. Some scholars think it was written in Jude's name by a later follower; others defend Jude's authorship.

destination: Not stated. Its many references to Israel's history and Jewish tradition suggest readers who knew them well.
purpose: To urge believers to "earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints" (1:3), to expose ungodly men who turned God's grace into an excuse for immorality and denied the Lord (1:4), and to call the readers to build themselves up in faith and keep themselves in God's love (1:20-23).
setting: Jude draws on Israel's history (the exodus, the angels who left their place, Sodom and Gomorrha, Cain, Balaam, Korah) and quotes a prophecy of Enoch (1:14-15) and an account of Michael disputing with the devil over Moses' body (1:9). These last two are found in Jewish writings outside the Bible (1 Enoch, and a work early Christians called the Assumption of Moses). Much of Jude is closely paralleled in 2 Peter 2.

outline.title: Why Jude writes: contend for the faith
Examples of judgment, and a portrait of the ungodly
Remember the apostles' words; keep yourselves in God's love
Doxology: him that is able to keep you

themes: The faith was "once delivered" and is to be defended (1:3).
God's grace is never a license for sin (1:4).
God judges, as Israel's history shows (1:5-7).
Believers keep themselves in God's love while he keeps them from falling (1:21, 1:24).
basis: From the letter's own text, compared with the Scriptures it draws on and 2 Peter; authorship and dating views summarized from standard introductions.
